# TileView

Header: `winui/ui/collections/TileView.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/collections/TileView.hpp`.

Templated items in wrapping rows of equal cells, virtualized and selectable.

Every cell is the size of the first item's container, or [set_item_width()](#set_item_width) and [set_item_height_cell()](#set_item_height_cell). A line holds as many cells as fit, or [maximum_rows_or_columns()](#maximum_rows_or_columns). Each item sits in a container with a backplate for hover and press, a 2 pixel accent frame when selected, and a check box in the top-right corner in Multiple mode. Items, templates, selection, drag reordering and scrolling come from [ListViewBase](list-view-base.md#uilistviewbase). When grouped ([set_group_keys()](list-view-base.md#set_group_keys)), each group header takes a line of its own and its cells start on the next.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: a 3-column picker of 96x96 tiles.
std::vector<std::string> names{"Red", "Green", "Blue", "Cyan", "Magenta", "Yellow"};
window.set_content(ui::TileView<std::string>{
    .items                   = names,
    .maximum_rows_or_columns = 3,
    .on_item_click           = [](const std::string& name) { std::println("picked {}", name); },
    .item                    = [](const std::string& name) -> ui::Spec {
        return ui::Text{.text = name, .width = 96.0f, .height = 96.0f};
    },
});

// Imperative:
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto grid  = std::make_unique<ui::TileViewControl>();
grid->set_item_template([](std::size_t i) { return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(std::to_string(i)); });
grid->set_item_count(12);
grid->set_item_width(100.0f);
grid->set_item_height_cell(64.0f);
grid->set_selection_mode(ui::SelectionMode::Multiple);
stack->add(std::move(grid));
```

## `ui::TileView`

Templated items in rows of equal cells. Builds a [ui::TileViewControl](#uitileviewcontrol).

It shares [ListViewBase](list-view-base.md#uilistviewbase) with [ui::ListView](list-view.md#uilistview). [`.items`](#uitileview-items), [`.item`](#uitileview-item) and [`.key`](#uitileview-key) take the same sources, and selection, click, drag and reorder work the same way. The cells wrap. [`.layout`](#uitileview-layout) swaps the equal cells for another arrangement and keeps everything else.

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<ui::Color>  swatches{ui::Color::from_rgb(0xE81123), ui::Color::from_rgb(0x0078D4),
                                 ui::Color::from_rgb(0x107C10), ui::Color::from_rgb(0xFFB900)};
ui::Property<ui::Color> picked{ui::colors::Black};

window.set_content(ui::TileView<ui::Color>{
    .items                   = swatches,
    .maximum_rows_or_columns = 4,
    .on_item_click           = [&](const ui::Color& color) { picked = color; },
    .item                    = [](const ui::Color& color) -> ui::Spec
    { return ui::Border{.background = color, .width = 40.0f, .height = 40.0f}; },
});
```

## `ui::TileViewControl`

Derives from `ui::ListViewBase`.

Templated items in wrapping rows of equal cells, virtualized and selectable.

Every cell is the size of the first item's container, or [set_item_width()](#set_item_width) and [set_item_height_cell()](#set_item_height_cell). A line holds as many cells as fit, or [maximum_rows_or_columns()](#maximum_rows_or_columns). Each item sits in a container with a backplate for hover and press, a 2 pixel accent frame when selected, and a check box in the top-right corner in Multiple mode. Items, templates, selection, drag reordering and scrolling come from [ListViewBase](list-view-base.md#uilistviewbase). When grouped ([set_group_keys()](list-view-base.md#set_group_keys)), each group header takes a line of its own and its cells start on the next.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: a 3-column picker of 96x96 tiles.
std::vector<std::string> names{"Red", "Green", "Blue", "Cyan", "Magenta", "Yellow"};
window.set_content(ui::TileView<std::string>{
    .items                   = names,
    .maximum_rows_or_columns = 3,
    .on_item_click           = [](const std::string& name) { std::println("picked {}", name); },
    .item                    = [](const std::string& name) -> ui::Spec {
        return ui::Text{.text = name, .width = 96.0f, .height = 96.0f};
    },
});

// Imperative:
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto grid  = std::make_unique<ui::TileViewControl>();
grid->set_item_template([](std::size_t i) { return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(std::to_string(i)); });
grid->set_item_count(12);
grid->set_item_width(100.0f);
grid->set_item_height_cell(64.0f);
grid->set_selection_mode(ui::SelectionMode::Multiple);
stack->add(std::move(grid));
```

### TileViewControl

```cpp
TileViewControl()
```

An empty grid in Single selection mode, horizontal orientation.

### set_layout

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_layout(std::unique_ptr<T> layout)
```

Replaces the layout that places the cells and returns an observer. The default is equal cells (a [TileLayoutEngine](item-layouts.md#class-tilelayoutengine)). Use a [WrapLayoutEngine](item-layouts.md#class-wraplayoutengine) for cells of their own width, or a [LinedFlowLayoutEngine](item-layouts.md#class-linedflowlayoutengine) for a photo wall. nullptr restores the default. With a layout that is not a [TileLayoutEngine](item-layouts.md#class-tilelayoutengine), the cell setters below have no effect, and the arrow keys find the item above or below by where the items are.

### maximum_rows_or_columns

```cpp
std::size_t maximum_rows_or_columns() const
```

The most cells per row (per column when Vertical); 0 (the default) is as many as fit.

### set_maximum_rows_or_columns

```cpp
void set_maximum_rows_or_columns(std::size_t max)
```

Caps the cells per row (per column when Vertical) and lays the view out again.

### orientation

```cpp
Orientation orientation() const
```

The fill direction; Horizontal by default.

### set_orientation

```cpp
void set_orientation(Orientation orientation)
```

Changes the fill direction, and the scroll axis with it, and lays the view out again.

### set_item_width

```cpp
void set_item_width(OptionalFloat width)
```

Sets the cell width in DIPs. nullopt, the default, takes the first item's width.

### set_item_height_cell

```cpp
void set_item_height_cell(OptionalFloat height)
```

Sets the cell height in DIPs. nullopt, the default, takes the first item's height. It has its own name because [ListViewBase::set_item_height()](list-view-base.md#set_item_height) sets the list container height.
